search_summary: Searches show fresh regulatory news with little dedicated advisory content: MAS's July 2026 Protected Cell Company consultation, updated MAS compliance toolkits (captive, SPRV, direct insurers, revised June 2026), MAS Circular ID 01/26 on ORSA submission lapses, and the AI governance rules phasing in from 2027. Competitor results are mostly generic law-firm or Big Four pages and job ads, so practical long-tail guides on licence types, timelines, ORSA lapses and the 2025 AML/CFT revisions are thin.

articles.title: MAS Protected Cell Company Framework: What Insurers and Captives Need to Know
articles.angle: Break down the July 2026 MAS PCC consultation and what it means for captives, reinsurers and ILS sponsors considering Singapore.
articles.search_evidence: MAS media release on the PCC consultation (7 July 2026) is the top 'MAS insurance Singapore 2026' result; no advisory-firm explainers appeared.

articles.title: MAS Circular ID 01/26: Avoiding Lapses in ORSA Report Submissions
articles.angle: Explain the circular's reminders, common causes of late or deficient ORSA submissions, and a pre-submission checklist.
articles.search_evidence: ORSA search surfaced MAS Circular ID 01/26 and MAS commentary on gaps in non-financial and group risk coverage; results otherwise were 2013-2014 vintage.

articles.title: Singapore Insurer Licence Types Explained: Direct, Reinsurer, Captive and Authorised Reinsurer
articles.angle: Side-by-side guide to choosing the right MAS licence route, with processing-time expectations (MAS up to 3 months vs. law-firm 6-8 week estimates).
articles.search_evidence: 'MAS licence application insurance' returns separate MAS pages per licence type with no comparison content, and conflicting timeline estimates.

articles.title: How to Use the MAS Compliance Toolkit for Insurers: A Practical Walkthrough
articles.angle: Show compliance teams how to turn the updated toolkits (revised Feb and June 2026) into an annual approvals, notifications and submissions calendar.
articles.search_evidence: 'Singapore insurance compliance 2026' top results are MAS toolkit PDFs for direct insurers, SPRVs and captives (revised June 2026) with no third-party guidance.

articles.title: 2025 AML/CFT Updates for Singapore Insurers: Proliferation Financing and STR Changes
articles.angle: Gap-assessment guide to the 1 July 2025 revisions, distinguishing Notice 314 (life) from the non-life/reinsurance guidelines.
articles.search_evidence: Clyde & Co and Allen & Gledhill coverage dominates; Swiss Life S$200,000 penalty shows enforcement risk; no practical implementation guides found.

articles.title: Singapore RBC2 Capital Requirements: A Practical Guide to Solvency Management
articles.angle: Focus on day-to-day capital management under Notice 133: solvency buffers, internal targets and optimisation levers, going beyond the framework overview already published.
articles.search_evidence: RBC2 results are dated 2016 consultation commentary and a single abrdn piece; MAS Notice 133 appears in 2026 results; current practical content is absent.

articles.title: Singapore AI Governance for Insurers: Preparing for the 2027 Compliance Phase-In
articles.angle: Readiness roadmap for insurers and intermediaries: AI inventory, third-party tool governance and board accountability ahead of October 2027.
articles.search_evidence: Insurance Business Asia article on AI governance rules before 2027 and MAS's March 2026 AI Risk Management Toolkit appeared; no consultancy-led guidance.
